title: HTML Attributes and Global Attributes
description: Learning how to use HTML attributes to control element behavior and styling.

flashcards.question: What are HTML attributes?
flashcards.answer: Additional information included inside an HTML tag that defines element behavior or appearance.

flashcards.question: Name some common global attributes.
flashcards.answer: id, class, style, title, data-*, tabindex, hidden.

flashcards.question: What is the purpose of the 'id' attribute?
flashcards.answer: It uniquely identifies an element within the document.

flashcards.question: How is the 'class' attribute used?
flashcards.answer: It groups elements for styling or scripting purposes.

flashcards.question: What does the 'title' attribute do?
flashcards.answer: Displays additional information as a tooltip on hover.

flashcards.question: Explain the use of 'data-*' attributes.
flashcards.answer: They store custom data private to the page or application for use in scripts.

flashcards.question: How does the 'style' attribute work?
flashcards.answer: It applies inline CSS styles directly to an element.

flashcards.question: What is the purpose of the 'hidden' attribute?
flashcards.answer: It hides the element from rendering on the page.

flashcards.question: Can attributes have boolean values? Give an example.
flashcards.answer: Yes, e.g., the 'disabled' attribute on form inputs disables the element.

flashcards.question: Why should you use global attributes?
flashcards.answer: They provide consistent control over behavior and appearance across all HTML elements.
